claims.scope: Conditionally describes interception of unencrypted network traffic; does not claim every adjacent Wi-Fi user can necessarily capture it.
Encryption and secret key need; early sequence is explicitly a result preview before handshake explanation.

claims.source: RFC8446 section 2; Khan Academy explanatory analogy
claims.scope: Exchange public shares while private material remains local; paint is illustrative, not a secure cryptosystem.
Server authentication is distinct from session key derivation; copied certificate alone cannot produce the required signature.
Actual local single-bit corruption raises InvalidTag and returns no plaintext.
HTTPS protects transport to website; website receives plaintext; no claim of end-to-end chat or mutually authenticated customer certificates.

visualAcceptanceChecks: Keep phone left and shop right throughout color demonstration.
Do not mix until s16; public yellow and private red/blue must remain distinguishable.
Exchange mixture cups, not the private source bottles.
Each final mixture uses equal total material and matching component proportions.
Show both final colors simultaneously for at least one second.
Certificate signing key and derived traffic key must remain visually distinguishable.
Tampering changes ciphertext byte 0 from 63 to 62, not a chosen plaintext word.
At website endpoint the original order is readable; transport intermediaries see ciphertext.
limitations: No real audience comprehension test conducted.
Reference video examined through transcript and selected playback screenshots only.
The paint sequence is illustrative, not a numerical or physical security proof.
